title: Give Copilot the Right Context
subtitle: Attach the smallest set of useful evidence in VS Code

scenes.title: Start with a broad question
scenes.body: A broad request makes the relevant evidence ambiguous.
scenes.narration: Ask “Why does zero pass validation?” in a fresh chat. Depending on the session, Copilot may already receive parts of the active editor or search the workspace. Look for the sources cited in its answer. Even a correct guess is easier to evaluate once you know where it came from. Next we will choose the evidence deliberately.
scenes.result: Check which sources are visible in this chat.
scenes.focus: The baseline answer reveals which sources were used
scenes.action: Start a fresh chat and check the response references.

scenes.title: Pick three useful inputs
scenes.body: The issue, function, and tests answer different questions.
scenes.narration: Select three things from the training checkout. The issue tells you what should happen. The validator tells you what the program does now. The test file tells you what behavior is already covered. If you only have the issue, you can explain the rule. With the source, you can identify exactly which comparison breaks it.
scenes.code:
Issue → expected behavior
Validator → current behavior
Tests → existing coverage
scenes.focus: The issue, function and test file answer distinct questions
scenes.action: Match each source to the question it answers.

scenes.title: Attach the source and test files
scenes.body: Use the context picker or a supported file mention.
scenes.narration: Open the validator and the test file in VS Code. Use the chat attachment control to add those files. Include the synthetic issue text and inspect the list before sending. Confirm the paths are from the checkout you intend to work on. This lets you and the assistant refer to the same function and the same tests.
scenes.code:
Attach order_quantity.py
Attach tests/test_order_quantity.py
Include the synthetic issue text.
scenes.result: The relevant function and tests are visible.
scenes.focus: All three current references appear in the request
scenes.action: Attach the issue and the two files in Copilot Chat.

scenes.title: Check the cited code
scenes.body: Verify the assistant's explanation against the actual file.
scenes.narration: Ask two questions together. “Why does zero pass, and which baseline test covers it?” The answer should show that greater than or equal to zero returns true for zero. Read the tests for one, five, and negative one. None runs the zero case. That gap explains why the existing suite can be green while the issue remains open.
scenes.code:
Explain why 0 is accepted.
Which existing test covers 0?
Name the relevant function and comparison.
scenes.result: Code allows 0. The baseline has no zero test.
scenes.focus: The comparison admits zero and no zero test exists yet
scenes.action: Check the cited source and test names in the editor.

scenes.title: Watch for outdated or broad context
scenes.body: Remove irrelevant context and attach the current file.
scenes.narration: Imagine an older attachment shows a greater-than comparison. The active checkout still has greater than or equal to zero. Open the current file and confirm the branch, then remove the stale attachment. Ask the question again using the current source. A one-character difference is enough to change the answer, so keep the two versions easy to distinguish.
scenes.code:
Check the branch and active file.
Remove unrelated attachments.
Attach the current implementation.
scenes.result: Use exact sources to resolve the mismatch.
scenes.focus: The current branch supplies the authoritative source for this run
scenes.action: Remove a stale attachment and reopen the current file.

scenes.title: Ask what is still missing
scenes.body: Make unknowns explicit before requesting a change.
scenes.narration: Try a follow-up where you provide the function but leave out the issue. Ask what the program does and what evidence would tell you whether that is correct. The code answers the first question. The issue answers the second. After you provide it, ask the assistant to compare the two and check that it keeps both claims tied to their sources.
scenes.code:
What evidence do you need for the expected behavior?
Use the supplied issue and code to compare them.
scenes.result: Requirement from issue. Behavior from source.
scenes.focus: The answer points to missing evidence when a source is absent
scenes.action: Ask which requirement source is still missing.

scenes.title: Compare two context sets
scenes.body: Explain what changed in the answer and why.
scenes.narration: Run the same question in two fresh sessions on the same branch. In the first attach the issue alone. In the second add the validator and tests. Compare their claims about the cause and coverage. Look for a real source line and a named test. Write one sentence about which attachment made each claim checkable.
scenes.code:
Run A: issue only.
Run B: issue + validator + tests.
Compare the cause and cited evidence.
scenes.result: A short comparison grounded in repository files.
scenes.focus: The stronger answer identifies the source line and test gap
scenes.action: Compare the two fresh-chat answers side by side.
